name: ARIANNA
full_name: Antarctic Ross Ice-Shelf ANtenna Neutrino Array
summary: A shallow-radio pilot programme on the Ross Ice Shelf tested autonomous stations and the use of the reflective ice–ocean boundary for neutrino detection.
detection_principle: Downward-facing log-periodic antennas listen for Askaryan impulses from neutrino-induced showers, including pulses reflected from the base of the ice shelf. Additional upward antennas help reject cosmic-ray air showers.

sites.name: Antarctica; Ross Ice Shelf and associated test sites
sites.location: Antarctica; Ross Ice Shelf and associated test sites

status.label: Research and development
status.evidence: Implemented pilot and subsequent R&D are documented; a full large-area ARIANNA observatory is not claimed operational.

timeline.event: Initial pilot stations deployed and first neutrino search performed.
Pilot performance, calibration and further station tests published.

collaboration.name: ARIANNA Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Second-generation electronics
key_parameters.value: Up to 2 Gsample/s digitisation with low-power autonomous operation

results.summary: Demonstrated low-noise autonomous radio operation and published UHE-neutrino flux limits. Large-area sensitivity projections do not imply the full proposed array was built.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
